newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
India admires efforts made by Sri Lankan government to achieve political solution to its 14-year old ethnic conflict, visiting Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral says in Colombo.
A total of 7,280 Asians, including an unspecified number of Sri Lankans, will be picked in the annual lottery for permanent residency in the United States, Washington-based attorney says.
India decides to remove quantitative restrictions and reduce tariff on 70 to 80 items of export interest to Sri Lanka, visiting Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral says in Colombo.
Nearly 400 Indian-built buses, bought under the Indian line of credit, arrives in Sri Lanka.
Air force Y-12 transport plane goes missing over the sea off northern Jaffna peninsula with four peoiple aboard.
Debris found scattered in immediate area believed to be that of missing aircraft.
India will not involve itself in Sri Lanka's internal affairs, External Affairs Minister Gujral says.
Sri Lanka Ports Authority announces it had suspended 185 temporary dock workers who took part in a strike which disrupted port work and warned of stern action against others.
Some 23 minority Tamil refugees land on south Indian coast on January 18.
Members of moderate Tamil party, the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), will meet visiting Indian External Affairs Minister Gujral on Tuesday.
